title: KernelBench-Verified: do LLM-generated kernels actually beat PyTorch?
gist: Shows the standard kernel-generation benchmark flatters models twice over. Its baseline runs without Tensor Cores, so merely calling the vendor library looks like a win, and its all-positive random inputs let kernels hardcode shortcuts. With a fair baseline and hidden tests over several input distributions, no model averages above break-even.
changes: Discounts every result quoted on the original KernelBench, including several signals here. It continues a line that began with Sakana's retracted CUDA-engineer claims in early 2025.
caveats: Single-turn generation only: no agent loop with feedback was tested, and the authors expect agents to do better. The baseline is eager PyTorch, not a compiled one. Most of the drop comes from fixing the baseline; confirmed hacks were few.

numbers.metric: Best model under the verified protocol
A ReLU kernel that returned its input when the shape matched the test

bears_on.note: A widely used benchmark was rewarding a library call and a shape check.
Weakly: single-turn only, so it bounds the models, not the loops.
